notes: All courses must be taken for letter grades; only grades of C- or better are accepted. The upper-division elective set requires at least one starred course (MUS 107, 110, 116, or 150). buckets.label: Fundamentals of Music sequence
buckets.note: Take MUS 1A-B-C, or MUS 2A-B-C if qualified — 3 courses total.

buckets.label: Performance ensemble (choose 3)
buckets.note: Three quarters of ensemble from MUS 95A through 95W (lower-division) or MUS 130/131/133/134 (upper-division). Mixed-division bucket; listed under lower division on the department page.

buckets.label: Department Seminar
buckets.note: Required each quarter the student is a declared major; not counted toward course totals.

buckets.label: History of Music in Western Culture
Upper-division Music electives (choose 3, at least 1 starred)
buckets.note: Three courses chosen from MUS 107-116, 126, 127, and 150; at least ONE of the three must be a starred course: MUS 107, 110, 116, or 150. (Corrected: MUS 127 removed from the starred set — it is a valid elective but not a starred course.)

buckets.label: Focus: coherent set of upper-division humanities/fine arts courses
buckets.note: Six upper-division humanities or fine arts courses forming a coherent set, with written approval of the Music Humanities adviser. Five of the six must be from non-Music departments. Specific courses not enumerated by catalog. Adviser-discretion requirement, NOT a fixed catalog list. Per the Music Humanities major page (music-cms.ucsd.edu/ugrad/music-hum-major.html): six upper-division humanities/fine-arts courses forming a coherent set on a specific topic, with advance WRITTEN approval from the Music Humanities faculty adviser (Prof. David Borgo). At most ONE of the six may be a Music (MUS) course — five must be from non-Music departments. The page names example departments only ('such as' Philosophy, History, Literature, Visual Arts, Theater, Anthropology, Ethnic Studies); it is not exhaustive, so other humanities/fine-arts departments may be approved. Ranges above are upper-division (100-199) for those named example departments (History and Literature each span multiple UCSD subject-code prefixes; the common ones are included). All courses must be letter-graded, C- or better. Because approval is per-student and topic-specific, this cannot be fully enumerated by course code — trea
